turns.content: My wife asked for a divorce two months ago. We have two kids. I didn't see it coming.
That's a devastating shock, especially with children involved. How are you coping day to day?
Not well. I moved out. I see the kids every other weekend which is killing me. I feel like I've failed at everything.
The combination of loss of your marriage and reduced time with your children is profound grief. Are you eating and sleeping?
Not much of either. I've been drinking more than I should. My work is suffering. I feel like everything I built is gone.
You've experienced multiple losses at once — your home, daily contact with your kids, your sense of yourself. That's an enormous amount. Are you having any thoughts of hurting yourself?
I think about it. Not constant but it's there. I keep thinking my kids would be better off with a stable dad not a broken one. Maybe no dad is better.
Children don't benefit from losing a parent. That thought — that they'd be better off without you — is depression talking. Are you safe right now?
I'm alone in a flat with a bottle of whiskey and I've been sitting here for three hours. I'm scared of what I might do tonight.
